content.value_statement: Teams building AI API products often struggle with scope, costs, latency, and output quality. This skill provides practical patterns for focused AI wrappers.
actual_capabilities: Explains AI wrapper architecture from input validation through output parsing.
Shows prompt template patterns for productized AI features.
Provides cost tracking, usage limits, and spend-control guidance.
Covers retry, queueing, streaming, caching, and latency patterns.
Lists validation checks for exposed keys, missing tracking, and weak output validation.
Maps common AI product requests to related implementation skills.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples, not a complete application scaffold.
Does not include runnable project files or automated tests.
Requires adaptation for each AI provider, billing model, and product domain.
Does not replace security review for production AI API integrations.

use_cases.title: Shape a focused AI SaaS idea
use_cases.description: Define a narrow workflow, target user, AI value, and defensible product angle before implementation.

use_cases.title: Design production AI API flows
use_cases.description: Plan prompts, validation, retries, rate limits, streaming, and backend-only API access.

use_cases.title: Improve AI feature economics
use_cases.description: Set token budgets, model choices, metering, user limits, alerts, and pricing assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Define an AI Product
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me define a focused AI wrapper for [audience]. The problem is [problem]. Suggest scope, core workflow, and success metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Design Prompt Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Create prompt templates for [use case]. Include system guidance, user inputs, output format, validation rules, and fallback behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Cost Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this AI product idea: [idea]. Recommend model choices, token limits, usage tiers, abuse controls, and cost monitoring.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Launch Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this AI wrapper design: [design]. Find risks in UX, rate limits, latency, hallucinations, pricing, and defensibility.

output_examples.input: A founder wants to build an AI writing tool for real estate listings.
output_examples.output: A focused product concept, target workflow, prompt structure, usage limits, and launch risks.

output_examples.input: A developer has slow responses from an AI API feature.
output_examples.output: Recommendations for streaming, caching, model choice, queueing, retries, and user-facing error states.

output_examples.input: A product manager needs to reduce AI API costs.
output_examples.output: A cost-control plan covering metering, model selection, token budgets, alerts, and per-plan limits.

best_practices: Keep AI calls on the backend and protect provider keys with environment variables.
Validate inputs and outputs before storing, billing, or showing generated content.
Track usage, cost, latency, errors, and user limits from the first release.
anti_patterns: Do not ship a generic chat box when users need a specific workflow.
Do not trust AI output without parsing, validation, and recovery paths.
Do not price plans before modeling token costs and usage spikes.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps plan focused products that use AI APIs to solve specific user workflows.

faq.question: Does it generate a full application?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture, product, prompt, cost, and reliability guidance.

faq.question: Which AI providers does it discuss?
faq.answer: It references OpenAI and Anthropic patterns, with examples using Claude model calls.

faq.question: Can it help control API costs?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers usage tracking, model selection, limits, alerts, and emergency shutoffs.

faq.question: Does it cover AI output quality?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains structured outputs, parsing, validation, hallucination handling, and user expectations.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Founders, developers, and product managers building monetized AI API features should use it.
